subject: Archaeology
title: The Library of Ashurbanipal
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Library of Ashurbanipal.

hook.text: An Assyrian king built the world's first organized library — 30,000 clay tablets covering everything from medicine to.

buildup.text: Ashurbanipal sent scribes across his empire to copy every text they could find. He wanted all knowledge in one place.

discovery.text: Layard found the library at Nineveh in 1852. The tablets had survived because fire baked the clay, preserving them.

twist.text: The library held the only complete copy of the Epic of Gilgamesh.

climax.text: The tablets are still being translated today. Thousands remain unread in museum basements — unknown stories waiting.

punchline.text: A tyrant saved the world's oldest literature.

quiz.question: How were Ashurbanipal's clay tablets accidentally preserved?
options: They were sealed in waterproof jars before the city fell
The fire that destroyed Nineveh baked the clay tablets, making them permanent
Scribes had coated them in a preservative resin before storage
